President of Lebanon Joseph Aoun, centre, and his wife, Nehmat Aoun, in Beirut, Lebanon, on December 2, 2025 [Adri Salido/Getty]By Al Jazeera Staff and AFPPublished On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has decried Iran’s meddling in Lebanon’s affairs and demanded Israel’s withdrawal from his country’s south.
In a speech on Saturday, on the eve of Lebanon’s 83rd independence anniversary, Aoun said Lebanon faces two interconnected fateful tests: the “Israeli occupation of parts of our land” and “foreign interference” from “some influential parties in the Iranian regime” through weapons and decisions outside the authority of the Lebanese state.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3World Bank official says Lebanon reconstruction making slow progresslist 2 of 3US steps up pressure on Iran-backed Hezbollah with new sanctionslist 3 of 3Can Israel’s opposition bloc stay united against Netanyahu?end of list
These “two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked” mean that Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence, he added.
“Withdraw from every inch of Lebanese territory. Stop your attacks. And return our captives,” Aoun demanded of Israel.
Dozens of Lebanese citizens are believed to be held in Israeli detention centres, including civilians as well as members of the Hezbollah armed group captured during fighting in southern Lebanon.
The president also pledged to press ahead with plans to bring all weapons under state control, declaring that there would be “no weapons outside the state that take orders from, or serve the interests of foreign powers.”
“You must hand over your weapons,” Aoun said.

The skyline of Manama, Bahrain [File: Frank Augstein/AP]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
Bahrain says an Iranian attack has struck a civilian industrial facility, starting a fire, in the latest escalation of the war in the Middle East.
Bahrain’s Defence Force said its air defences intercepted a number of Iranian aerial attacks late on Saturday.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Bahrain thwarts drone attack; Iran claims targeting US radarlist 2 of 3‘Too early’ to determine impact of US blockade on Iran, with Tehran defiantlist 3 of 3US targets Iran’s ship-to-ship transfers: Can Tehran break the blockade?end of list
In a post on X, Bahrain’s Ministry of Interior said the attack was part of “Iranian aggression”.
It said preliminary reports pointed to material damage but no injuries, and that civil defence teams were working to bring the fire under control.
The Interior Ministry did not name the facility or say where it was. Earlier, air raid sirens sounded in Bahrain, and the ministry urged residents to move to the nearest safe place without saying what the threat was.
In a statement after the attack, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had carried out a combined missile and drone operation targeting United States military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain.
The IRGC claimed it destroyed two US Patriot air defence radars at the bases.
The attack was “in response to continued aggression and violations of the airspace of the Islamic Republic of Iran”, the statement said.
“After two US MQ-1 and MQ-9 reconnaissance and combat drones violated Iranian airspace, US military positions at the aforementioned bases were targeted in an operation by the IRGC Aerospace Force,” it added.

Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro gestures after taking medical tests at DF Star hospital in Brasilia on August 16, 2025 [File: AFP]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
Brazil’s former President Jair Bolsonaro is in intensive care after being diagnosed with an acute bowel obstruction, according to the DF Star hospital where he is being treated.
Bolsonaro, 71, was admitted on Friday with abdominal pain. In a bulletin on Saturday, the hospital said doctors have started giving him fluids and nutritional support, and inserted a tube into his stomach.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Flávio Bolsonaro vows to continue father’s political fight in Brazillist 2 of 3Lula visits ailing Chief Raoni as Brazil recognises Indigenous landlist 3 of 3Rubio says Trump administration did not help Bolsonaro flee Brazil to USend of list
It said the former president is clinically stable and conscious, although they said there was no projected date for his discharge.
“There is hope that his condition will improve,” his son, Senator-elect Carlos Bolsonaro, wrote on X on Saturday afternoon. “He is being closely monitored and is fighting to get his bowels working again, with his usual grit and focus.”
In the early hours of Saturday morning, he described his father’s difficult night of treatment, where food residue was removed from his stomach using a tube inserted into his nose, and bouts of nausea.
“I’m not a doctor, but I’ve never seen him like this,” he wrote, suggesting that his father might need another surgery, which would be his 10th in less than eight years.

Iran says Qatari mediators have travelled to Tehran as the country’s foreign minister urges the United States to accept Iranian conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
News of the talks came as the commander of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) toured an underground missile facility on Saturday and the country’s president said Iran is facing a “silent economic war”.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3US targets Iran’s ship-to-ship transfers: Can Tehran break the blockade?list 2 of 3Iran says it downed US drones over Hormuz as bid to end war remains stalledlist 3 of 3Qatar’s emir calls for diplomacy to end regional conflictsend of list
A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Friday night and held two hours of talks with Iranian officials, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said, according to Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency.
“We are in contact with mediators, including the Qataris, both in person and virtually, and are holding the necessary discussions to see whether another opportunity can be given to diplomacy,” he said on Saturday.
The US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to launch strikes against Israel and Gulf states hosting US military bases. ⁠The conflict has drawn in countries across the region, disrupted shipping and ⁠pushed up global energy prices.
Gharibabadi said the talks have not yet become formal negotiations. If they do, the technical details of Iran’s nuclear programme would be discussed, he added, but Iran’s position is that its enriched uranium must not leave the country.

People chant slogans during a trade union protest demanding higher wages and pensions and relief from rising living costs in Lisbon, Portugal, on November 21, 2026 [Pedro Nunes/Reuters]By Al Jazeera Staff, AP and ReutersPublished On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
Thousands of people have taken to the streets across Europe to protest against rising living costs, unaffordable housing and cuts to public services, as students and workers demand action from their governments.
Demonstrators marched across France and Portugal on Saturday, following youth-led protests in several European countries on Friday.
Recommended Stories list of 2 itemslist 1 of 2French police officers guilty of Michel Zecler assault: What happens now?list 2 of 2UK police drag man from protest over ‘Pallet Sign Acton’ shirtend of list
The gatherings reflect overlapping concerns about economic insecurity, education and future opportunities, although their demands and scale differ considerably between countries.
In France, the Ministry of Interior said 82,500 people joined demonstrations nationwide on Saturday, including 21,500 in Paris, down from 106,000 the previous weekend. Organisers estimated a higher turnout of 150,000.
The protests, now in their sixth consecutive weekend, began in September with students demanding better schools before expanding to include trade unions and the Yellow Vests, a movement that emerged in 2018 over rising fuel prices and living costs.
